extracted.intended_audience: aspiring fiction writers and members of The Write Practice community who want to practice 'show, don't tell'
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and a timed writing prompt to help creative writers practice showing emotion/character through concrete detail, sensory language, and action rather than stating feelings. Includes revision tips and a community guessing exercise to test effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show, don't tell — core principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't tell your reader what to think. Show the emotion and let the reader feel it. ("Don't tell me the moon is shining; show me the glint of light on broken glass." — Anton Chekhov)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let the reader decide if your protagonist is scared; rather than writing 'She was scared,' demonstrate fear through behavior and environment (e.g., hiding under covers, wetting the bed, jumping into bed so monsters can't grab legs). Don't instruct the reader; evoke the feeling via scene details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the five senses
rubrics_metrics.description: You can show by using your five senses. What does it smell like, feel like? What does your protagonist hear?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make your writing come alive with sensory details so readers experience the scene: smells, textures, sounds, tastes, and visual particulars create immersion rather than flat statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid verbs and body language
rubrics_metrics.description: Use vivid verbs to describe your character's body language (for example: fists may be clenched, teeth gritted, lips curled).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptive physical actions and strong verb choices help readers visualize and feel the scene; prefer active, specific verbs over generic or passive phrasing to show emotion and intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show traits with specific, concrete details (avoid generic labels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of telling a character is a carpenter, show she is a carpenter by describing her using her dual-bevel, sliding, compound miter saw.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete objects, tools, and domain-specific details to imply professions, skills, and background rather than labeling the character directly; specificity builds credibility and economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision test: highlight adjectives and feelings to find telling
rubrics_metrics.description: As you revise your manuscript, highlight adjectives and feelings. These words reveal when you're telling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monica M. Clark's strategy: highlighting words that name emotions or rely on adjectives exposes passages where you told rather than showed; then replace those with actions, sensory detail, or concrete imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telling has a place — use it deliberately
rubrics_metrics.description: Telling is stating information, and sometimes you will tell in a story. You might want to tell us your protagonist is a carpenter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize when straightforward information serves economy or clarity; balance telling with showing so that essential facts are communicated without losing reader immersion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice with timed prompts and community feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose an emotion (or adjective) and write for fifteen minutes to show that feeling; post the piece and let readers guess what you were trying to show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exercise trains showing by forcing concrete choices under time pressure and uses reader guesses as a diagnostic: if readers identify the intended emotion, your showing worked. Be kind when commenting and offer guesses/feedback on others' pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show specific emotions through concrete behaviors/examples
rubrics_metrics.description: For emotions like sadness, anger, fear, and surprise, use concrete behaviors instead of naming the feeling (e.g., sadness: staying in bed, not showering, eating only potato chips; anger: throwing pots or going silent; fear: hiding, quick movements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate lists of observable behaviors or small habits that communicate an interior state; apply those behaviors in scenes to let readers infer the emotion without explicit labels.
